T
VZ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Today's big story: Anthropic Broke Its $83 IPO Price. What Did Facebook Do Next?

T-Mobile US closed at $166.25 on Wednesday. Adjusted for dividends, that is 23.6% below its highest close of the past year, reached on March 6. Counting dividends, the shares returned -17.5% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 8.4%. The past month was kinder: the stock rose 14% as the index fell 6.9%.

The business has kept paying its owners through that slide. On its October 28 call, management said T-Mobile had bought back $10.3 billion of its shares this year through October 23. It had also raised its dividend per share by 15%. At Wednesday's close, the dividend alone works out to a 2.5% yield.

T-Mobile raised its dividend per share by 15%, yet the shares returned -17.5% over the past year, counting dividends. If you own it for the income, that is a fall you had to sit through to collect each payment. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

So the cash is there. What could make the stock itself worth meaningfully more? One candidate sits outside the phone plans T-Mobile is known for: internet service for the home. Management has set targets for it out to 2030. To lift the stock, T-Mobile has to keep signing home customers at rising prices. And enough of the extra cash has to reach shareholders while the company bids for new airwaves in 2027 and 2028.

Is T-Mobile's home internet business still growing?

By management's account, yes. But T-Mobile does not publish the customer numbers you would need to check it. Most of its home customers use 5G broadband, which is internet sent over the same wireless network as its phones. On the call, management said it was "tracking really well ahead of pace to our goal of hitting 15 million customers by 2030." It does not disclose how many customers it added, only that its additions led the industry in the quarter ended September 2026.

The prices point the same way. Management said 5G broadband revenue per customer rose from a year earlier and from the quarter before. Its smaller fiber business reached "approximately 20% 12-month penetration." and customer growth sped up. Management also said it was well on track toward its target of 3 million to 4 million fiber customers by 2030.

The first proof for the whole company shows up in revenue per account, which counts everything a household pays T-Mobile. Management raised its forecast for 2026 growth in that figure to about 3.5%, up from 2.5% to 3%. It credited premium phone plans first. It named selling 5G broadband and fiber to existing accounts as part of the rest. So home internet is helping, but it shares the credit.

Berenberg Just Cut Its AST SpaceMobile Target From $92 to $30 ©@3DSculptor from Getty Images via Canva, @metamorworks from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Berenberg downgraded AST SpaceMobile to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $30 from $92, citing satellite launch delays.

Three BlueBirds are still waiting on a launch date from SpaceX, and the next three are booked on Blue Origin's New Glenn, which hasn't flown since an explosion on its pad in May.

Analysts have cut their 2027 revenue estimate to $561 million from $748 million at the end of June, and their expected 2027 loss has widened to $1.65 a share from $1.05.

The Hold looks right while estimates keep falling, and the next tests are AST's US service with AT&T by year-end and New Glenn's return to flight.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) is down 80% from its May high, and Berenberg just stopped calling it a buy. On Nov. 27, the firm downgraded the stock to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $30 from $92.

The problem is rockets. BlueBirds 14 to 16 are still waiting on a launch date from SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ), and the next three are booked on Blue Origin's New Glenn, which hasn't flown since an explosion on its pad in May. AST also plans to switch on intermittent US service with AT&T (T:NYSE) before year-end.

Launches keep slipping

AST's target of about 45 BlueBirds in orbit has slipped to mid-2027. Its own rocket, Blacklift, isn't due to fly until late 2028. Until then, AST leans on SpaceX.

Berenberg says its Buy came too early

Berenberg initiated coverage with a Buy in September and now calls that rating premature. It expects a funded constellation of about 100 satellites by 2028. Analyst Michael Filatov still likes the technology, but "the path to scale depends on launch capacity ASTS does not control." A successful New Glenn return to flight would make him revisit it.

title: Tutor Perini (TPC) Shows Fast-paced Momentum But Is Still a Bargain Stock

Momentum investing is essentially an exception to the idea of "buying low and selling high." Investors following this style of investing are usually not interested in betting on cheap stocks and waiting long for them to recover. Instead, they believe that "buying high and selling higher" is the way to make far more money in lesser time.

Who doesn't like betting on fast-moving trending stocks? But determining the right entry point isn't easy. Often, these stocks lose momentum once their valuation moves ahead of their future growth potential. In such a situation, investors find themselves loaded up on expensive shares with limited to no upside or even a downside. So, going all-in on momentum could be risky at times.

It could be safer to invest in bargain stocks that have been witnessing price momentum recently. While the Zacks Momentum Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to trends in a stock's price or earnings, is pretty useful in identifying great momentum stocks, our 'Fast-Paced Momentum at a Bargain' screen comes handy in spotting fast-moving stocks that are still attractively priced.

Tutor Perini (TPC) is one of the several great candidates that made it through the screen. While there are numerous reasons why this stock is a great choice, here are the most vital ones:

Investors' growing interest in a stock is reflected in its recent price increase. A price change of 9.7% over the past four weeks positions the stock of this construction company well in this regard.

While any stock can see a spike in price for a short period, it takes a real momentum player to deliver positive returns for a longer time frame. TPC meets this criterion too, as the stock gained 3.7% over the past 12 weeks.

Moreover, the momentum for TPC is fast paced, as the stock currently has a beta of 2.12. This indicates that the stock moves 112% higher than the market in either direction.

Given this price performance, it is no surprise that TPC has a Momentum Score of B, which indicates that this is the right time to enter the stock to take advantage of the momentum with the highest probability of success.

In addition to a favorable Momentum Score, an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions has helped TPC earn a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Our research shows that the momentum-effect is quite strong among Zacks Rank #1 and #2 stocks. That's because as covering analysts raise their earnings estimates for a stock, more and more investors take an interest in it, helping its price race to keep up. How Much Money Each Yield Level Demands

A moderate 6% yield comes from REITs, preferreds, and covered call funds. At a moderate 6% yield, $133,200 divided by 0.06 equals $2,220,000. Dividend growth slows, and some of these strategies cap your upside.

At an aggressive 10% from BDCs and leveraged closed-end funds, $133,200 divided by 0.10 equals $1,332,000. Cuts are more common, and principal can erode.

An 8.3% Blueprint Built on About $1.6 Million

title: Have AT&T's Dividends Been Worth It?

Have AT&T's Dividends Been Worth It?

Image from Pixabay

AT&T sells wireless plans and fiber internet. It pays part of the cash it earns to holders as dividends. Over the past year alone, dividends added about 4.3 percentage points to the stock's return. A percentage point is the plain difference between two returns. The share price, though, has trailed the market. So what did a five-year holder end up with once every dividend is counted?

How Far Has AT&T Stock Trailed The Market?

On price alone, AT&T stock rose 22.8% from November 17, 2021 to November 25, 2026. The S&P 500 rose 53.1% over the same dates. That left AT&T 30.3 percentage points behind. A holder who watched only the price saw the market pull far ahead.

AT&T trailed the market by 30.3 points on its share price alone. If you rely on this one stock to pay your bills, its cash payouts, not its share price, have carried most of your return. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

How Much Did AT&T's Dividends Add?

With dividends reinvested, AT&T returned 62.5% over the same five years. Reinvested means each payment bought more shares. The dividends added 39.7 percentage points to the price gain. Most of the holder's result came from the dividends, not the share price.

Did The Dividends Close The Gap For AT&T Holders?

The table sets AT&T beside the S&P 500, first on price alone and then with dividends.

The market pays dividends too. With them counted, the S&P 500 returned 63.7%. That leaves AT&T just 1.2 percentage points behind. AT&T's dividends closed almost all of the gap with the market.

What This Means If You Own AT&T For Income

AT&T did pay out more than the market. Over the past year, its dividends added 4.3 points to its return, against 1.2 points for the market's dividends. Over five years, AT&T's larger payments made up for nearly all of the gap its slower share price left.

The cash comes from its phone and internet business, the Communications segment. It brought in 96.2% of revenue in 2025, the year to December 31. In the four quarters to September 30, 2026, AT&T produced $17.8 billion of free cash flow. That is the cash left after running and investing in the business. It paid $7.94 billion in dividends over the same quarters.

The company's October 21 earnings release guides to an annual dividend of $1.11 a share for 2026. A past dividend is a record, not a promise. For an income holder, the test to keep checking is whether AT&T's return with dividends keeps pace with the S&P 500's with dividends.

Key Takeaways

AT&T stock is up 10% in the past month as the broader market fell and investors moved into cheap, high-yielding stocks.

SpaceX wants to build a fourth US carrier, but the Boost Mobile network it wants to buy runs on AT&T and T-Mobile, which reportedly plan to cut it off.

AT&T's free cash flow covers its dividend more than twice over, and the stock trades at 9.0x forward earnings, right at its 5-year average.

Steve Eisman's "uninvestable" call looks too harsh on AT&T, though AST SpaceMobile's satellite rollout and fourth-quarter churn will show how the SpaceX fight plays out.

AT&T (T:NYSE) stock rose 10% in the month to its Nov. 25 close, while the S&P 500 fell 6% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 10%.

After the close on Oct. 22, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) was seeking access to at least 80,000 US cell sites to become a fourth carrier, and AT&T and T-Mobile US (TMUS:NASDAQ) each fell about 8% the next day. Since then, both have reportedly pushed back on SpaceX, and AT&T has leaned on its satellite partner, AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ).

Not everyone's buying the rebound. On the Nov. 6 episode of The Real Eisman Playbook, Steve Eisman said of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile: "I think the big three are just uninvestable."

Income buyers came back

With no big company news, AT&T rode investors' move into steady, high-yielding stocks as tech sold off: Walmart rose 10%, McDonald's 14% and Campbell's more than 15% over the same stretch. Buyers had reason to like AT&T's third quarter. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.65 from $0.54 a year earlier, management raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to about $2.40 from $2.25-$2.35, and it kept its plan for $18 billion-plus of free cash flow. (Management credits most of that raise to halting depreciation on the Mexico unit it's selling.)

Analysts expect normalized EPS to keep rising, from $2.12 in 2025 to $2.93 in 2028:

AT&T (T): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

That's about 11% a year, in line with AT&T's own double-digit guidance.

TIKR tracks 24 analysts on AT&T. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AT&T, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AT&T's Analyst Ratings

SpaceX is coming, slowly

The threat is real. Qualcomm's CEO said on its Nov. 4 call that SpaceX chose Qualcomm for a nationwide land-based 5G network starting in 2027, and The Washington Post reported that SpaceX was in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile. But Boost leases network access from AT&T and T-Mobile, and Semafor reported on Nov. 5 that both would cut Boost off if SpaceX bought it. Even Elon Musk said at the DealBook Summit on Nov. 18: "I don't think this means… AT&T, Verizon, others go out of business or anything."
